title: Claude Code
summary: A coding agent with terminal and IDE entry points for repository work.

sources.title: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP

facts.label: Workflow
facts.value: Terminal, IDE, desktop and web coding agent

facts.label: Privacy / data handling
facts.value: Consumer training settings and commercial terms differ; confirm the account type and opt-in settings.

facts.label: Product self-hosting
facts.value: Claude Code cloud sessions can run on organization-operated self-hosted environments with customer-managed runners. The feature is public beta for Team and Enterprise and off by default. This describes session compute, not model hosting: model inference still goes outbound to api.anthropic.com. No account configuration was checked.

facts.label: Local model inference
facts.value: For self-hosted cloud sessions, Anthropic says model inference is outbound HTTPS to api.anthropic.com and cannot be routed through Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry or an LLM gateway. The official docs reviewed do not describe an on-device local-model route for other Claude Code surfaces; custom endpoint compatibility and account-specific options remain unverified.

facts.label: Code / data portability
facts.value: Claude Code works in a project directory and directly with Git. Its session checkpoints can restore file edits made through Claude's editing tools, but do not track Bash-command changes or reliably capture subagent and external/concurrent edits; Anthropic recommends Git for permanent version history. This documents repository-file portability, not session or settings migration.

facts.label: MCP support
facts.value: Claude Code documents local stdio and remote HTTP, SSE and WebSocket MCP server connections; project-scoped servers require workspace trust and approval.

sections.heading: Separate session compute from model inference
paragraphs: Team and Enterprise organizations can run cloud sessions on self-hosted runners during the public beta, but the feature is off by default and still sends model inference to Anthropic's API. Confirm plan eligibility, enablement, network path and applicable data terms before treating a self-hosted runner as an isolation boundary.

sections.heading: Constrain command execution
paragraphs: Start with a repository branch and a specific acceptance test. Inspect proposed commands, file changes and network access before accepting a result. Keep production credentials outside the trial and verify that the task can be rolled back.

sections.heading: Check the account route
paragraphs: Determine whether the session uses a subscription, direct API billing or another supported provider. The applicable spending and data policies follow that account route. A displayed token estimate is not automatically a subscription invoice.

pros.text: Organizations can route Claude Code cloud sessions to runners on infrastructure they operate, keeping repository checkouts and build artifacts within that environment.
The MCP documentation covers local stdio servers and remote HTTP or WebSocket servers.

cons.text: Self-hosted environments are a public beta for Team and Enterprise, are off by default, and still send inference to Anthropic; they are not a local-model mode.
The SSE transport is deprecated; the documentation recommends HTTP when the server supports it.
Project MCP server approvals depend on workspace trust; a cloned repository cannot approve its own servers.

faqs.question: Does a Claude Code self-hosted environment keep model inference on your infrastructure?
faqs.answer: No. Anthropic documents self-hosted runners for cloud-session compute, while model inference still goes outbound to api.anthropic.com. The feature is a public beta for Team and Enterprise and is off by default; no account configuration was checked.

faqs.question: Can Claude Code use a local model?
faqs.answer: The official docs reviewed do not document an on-device local-model route. For self-hosted cloud sessions, model inference still goes to Anthropic's API; custom endpoints and options for other surfaces remain unverified.

faqs.question: Can Claude Code work be recovered outside the session?
faqs.answer: Claude Code works with project files and Git, but its checkpoints are session recovery rather than permanent version history. Anthropic says Bash-command changes and some subagent or external edits are not tracked, and recommends Git for durable history.

faqs.question: Which MCP transports does Claude Code document?
faqs.answer: It documents local stdio and remote HTTP or WebSocket. SSE is deprecated and HTTP is recommended where available.

faqs.question: Can a cloned project approve its own MCP servers?
faqs.answer: No. Repository project-server approvals are not read from checked-in settings until the workspace is trusted; the cloned repository cannot approve those servers itself.

verdict: Shortlist Claude Code when an explicit repository task and command-based verification fit your workflow. Review command permissions and the account billing route first.
bestFor: Developers comfortable inspecting changes and command results
notFor: Users expecting autonomous changes to be safe without review
migration: Keep build instructions and acceptance tests in the repository. Port tool-specific rules deliberately and review permissions again in the replacement.
